decision: Option B — approve supplied Markdown/text export as canonical frozen source artifact
artifact_type: UTF-8 Markdown/text export of the Project Madurai page
approval_basis: The supplied artifact retains the Project Madurai title, contributor and rights header, all 400 numbered record identities, printed metadata, canonical literary text, loss statement, lacuna markers, and closing statement.
The user explicitly authorized formal documentation of the supplied export as the canonical frozen artifact when exact HTML preservation is impossible.
The artifact is checksum-pinned, preserved unchanged, parsed deterministically, and validated at 400/400 body and 400/400 source-note equality.
limitations: The artifact is not the original HTTP response bytes and cannot certify original HTML markup, element boundaries, attributes, or byte-level identity with pmuni0057.html.
HTML-specific layout evidence is unavailable; parser boundaries rely on explicit printed labels and retained blank-line structure in the supplied export.
A later raw-HTML acquisition would be a separate source object and must not silently replace this frozen source identity.
freeze_acceptance: Acceptable for corpus schema 1.0.0 as a source-faithful transcription layer because the frozen claim is limited to this exact supplied artifact and does not claim raw-HTML preservation or critical-edition authority.
